content: Made pizza dough this weekend using my sourdough discard. I usually throw the discard away but I figured the flavor profile would work for a longer-fermented pizza dough.
Sourdough discard pizza dough is great — you get the tangy flavor without needing to plan around the starter's peak. How did you adjust the recipe for the discard?

I replaced about 20% of the flour and water with discard, added commercial yeast since the discard isn't at peak activity, and bumped the hydration percentage to 68% for a crispier crust. The thing is, the discard adds a slight sourness that plays really well with the tomato sauce.

That's a nice balance — the commercial yeast handles the leavening reliability while the discard contributes flavor. 68% hydration should give you good extensibility for stretching without being too wet to handle.

Exactly. I cold-fermented the dough balls for 48 hours which developed even more flavor. Baked on a preheated steel at 550°F — the crust was perfectly leopard-spotted with great spring. Fundamentally pizza dough is simpler than bread dough but the variables still matter — temperature, hydration, fermentation time.
